fable.summary:
Review complete. No files were edited, no commits made, no refs fetched, no delegation.

## Verdict

The coordinator's evidence is sound where it exists. I independently re-ran ancestry, rename-aware diffs and blob comparisons from the bare repositories and reproduced the recorded result: only three in-scope file changes across all 32 direct sources, all in pstack. Matt's eleven sources have zero in-scope changes. The one real correction concerns inventory completeness, not the deltas.

**Inventory gap.** Local origin.txt files contain 41 sources pointing at mattpocock/skills or cursor/plugins. The inventory lists 33 of them plus one unrelated mblode record. Eight cursor/plugins sources are absent and were not marked contextual either:

- `commit/cursor-reviewable-pr`, `pr/cursor-reviewable-pr`, `pr-followup/cursor-ci-followup`, `report-work-activity/cursor-period-summary`, `review-code-changes/cursor-quality-review`, `simplify-code/cursor-deslop` under cursor-team-kit/
- `pr-followup/dyl-pr-readiness` under dyl-stack/
- `review-code-changes/thermos-review` under thermos/

All eight are non-pstack authors, so excluding them matches the strict reading of "poteto (pstack)". But `review-code-changes/dyl-review` was included as contextual while `dyl-pr-readiness` from the same author was dropped, and the `commit` skill is missing from the frozen local set. I verified from cursor.git that no cursor-team-kit, dyl-stack or thermos path changed between 23e4138 and e43c7ee, so the omission changes no finding. The report should still list them as explicitly out of scope with that evidence, so the user sees how "either" was interpreted.

**Everything else verified.** Both bare repos have refs/heads/main equal to the recorded candidates with SSH remotes. Every cursor is an ancestor of its candidate. The actual commit chain is 7022c81, 23e4138, 9511e60, a586282, e43c7ee. No renames or copies appear with -M -C in any range. Matt's only deletions are consumed changeset files. LICENSE blobs are identical at every pin in both repos. The 159 frozen local files match the working tree byte for byte. HEAD matches the snapshot and the only working-tree change is the pre-existing walkthrough deletion.

## Classification of recorded deltas

| Owner and source | Change | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| design-code-structure / pstack-architect | architect/SKILL.md screen sentence replaced; design-red-flags.md adds four flags | Adapt, see below |
| error-handling / pstack-boundaries-and-recovery | plugin.json version 0.15.7 to 0.15.9 only | Skip |
| All 30 other direct sources | scoped blobs identical | No relevant change |

The architect delta, commit a586282, replaces "Reject or revise shallow modules, information leakage, temporal decomposition, and pass-through methods" with "Assume the next contributor is an agent that sees only the files it opened, copies the nearest example, and takes the shortest path that compiles. Prefer the design where a change that looks right from one file is right for the whole repo." The reference adds Split ownership, Two ways to do one task, Importable internals and Hand-synced list.

Against the local text:

- **Split ownership** is already covered. `design-code-structure/references/state-and-boundaries.md:24-28` names single-writer enforcement for shared mutable state, and `SKILL.md:146-148` treats unexpected shared writes as friction evidence. Skip or add a one-clause pointer.
- **Partial-context contributor lens** is new. `SKILL.md:94-100` compares on change locality and reading effort but never asks whether a change that looks right from one file is right repo-wide. Adapt as one comparison criterion, actor-neutral.
- **Two ways to do one task** is partially covered by "repeated policy" at `SKILL.md:102` and "duplicated policy" at `SKILL.md:147`. The missing part is the explicit screen for parallel supported paths that keep gaining callers.
- **Hand-synced list** is partially covered by "Avoid storing values that can be derived reliably" at `SKILL.md:74`. Missing: a parallel list as a design smell and the derive-or-fail-the-build remedy.
- **Importable internals** is partially covered by "private representations exposed to callers" at `SKILL.md:102`. The toolchain-enforced boundary idea is absent locally. `typescript-best-practices/references/compiler-and-modules.md:21-24` tests advertised entrypoints but does not say to make internals unreachable.

## Contextual and newly discovered material

**Matt, outside every recorded path.** Commits c5b9869 and PR 1121 change `skills/engineering/ask-matt/SKILL.md` and `docs/engineering/diagnosing-bugs.md` to say post-fix reflection is a user-invoked retro step the skill never calls itself. The diagnosing-bugs SKILL.md blob is identical at both commits, and the hand-off removal itself landed 2026-08-15, before the cursor.
